messages:

Subject: Quick Q on where our inference data is actually processed

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo on Wednesday — really helpful. Before we go deeper, Legal wants a concise picture of where inference payloads will be processed when we use Redwood (hosted API for now). Specifically:

1) Can you confirm which cloud regions and third-party subprocessors could process or transiently hold request/response payloads for an EU customer?
2) Do you ever hand off payloads to analytics or logging vendors outside the EU?
3) If we sign for a Dedicated or Private deployment, can we guarantee EU-only execution and deletion by default?
4) Typical deletion timelines for logs, cached KV entries, and backups once a deletion request is issued?

We need a short write-up we can give Legal and our security reviewer (1–2 pages). If you have a simple diagram or inventory, that would be great.

Best,
Elena

Head of Infrastructure, Geonova AI
elena.novak@geonova.ai

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where our inference data is actually processed

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a one-page residency map and our subprocessor inventory export for quick review.

1) Regions & cloud hops (hosted API):
- Primary execution is in the region you select at request time; EU customers default to our eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 clusters.
- If a specific model version is only available in another region, we automatically fall back to the closest compatible EU replica; we do not route EU customer inference to non-EU regions except in explicit cross-border fallback scenarios (which we document in the routing policy).
- Transient hops: load balancer, edge proxy (for TLS termination and routing), and internal autoscaler/queueing components can see request metadata (request id, model id, timestamp) but not decrypted customer secrets.

2) Third-party subprocessors (hosted API):
- Examples: cloud provider (VM/GPU host), object store for ephemeral checkpoints, CDN for model wheel distribution, logging provider (aggregated telemetry), and monitoring SaaS.
- We do not send customer request payloads to analytics vendors for processing. Aggregated telemetry (non-PII operational metrics) may be sent to monitoring/logging tools; payload content stays within our runtime. See attached CSV for current vendor names and contract locales.

3) Dedicated / Private deployments:
- Dedicated: you get reserved capacity in the region(s) you subscribe to — we can commit to EU-only physical capacity for the Dedicated contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full EU-only execution is achievable; control plane can be either Redwood-hosted with region pinning or fully customer-hosted. For air-gapped on-prem installs, there is zero egress to Redwood-managed subprocessors.

4) Deletion timelines (typical):
- Immediate logical deletion from serving KV cache: within seconds of a successful API-driven delete request or account deactivation.
- Asynchronous background wipe of logs/metrics that reference token-level traces: 24–72 hours (aggregated telemetry retains no raw input by design).
- Backups / cold snapshots: typically 30 days retention window and securely purged according to retention policy; we can accelerate on contract.

Attachments: residency-map.pdf (1 page), subprocessors-inventory.csv (export; includes region column).

If you’d like, Marissa in Trust & Safety can add the contractual language for the SLA and deletion carve-outs — looping her in.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Hi Elena / LegalOps — Marissa on Trust & Safety here, thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick clarifications for contract and audit language: 

A) Cross-border fallback definition & notification:
- Fallback trigger examples: (i) regional capacity exhaustion (sustained >90% utilization for 30s+ causing queuing); (ii) a regional hardware outage that affects availability; (iii) customer-requested temporary failover for disaster recovery testing.
- Notification model: for production traffic we will: (1) attempt to route to a compatible EU replica first; (2) if non-EU fallback is required we will notify the customer's technical contact via email and the Console incident banner within 5 minutes of the event; (3) provide an incident report with timeline and root cause within 48 hours.

B) Telemetry & stripping rules:
- Operational metrics: timestamps, request size, model id, token counts, latency percentiles, and non-human-readable hashes of request ids. These are safe for aggregation and may be sent to monitoring/logging vendors.
- We do not export raw request/response text, embeddings, or PII-like fields to third-party analytics vendors. Where telemetry touches identifiers, we pseudonymize using HMAC with a Redwood-managed key (or customer-managed key for Private deployments).

C) Contractual commitments for Dedicated:
- We can include a clause that prohibits cross-border routing of your production inference requests without prior written consent; standard Dedicated SOW language covers region pinning and cross-border exceptions. We will add a specific redline for "EU physical execution and no cross-border egress for production inference requests unless Customer consents in writing."

D) Subprocessor audits / SOC2 evidence ownership:
- Primary contact for audit/subprocessor evidence: marissa_cole@redwood.ai. Send SOC2 evidence requests to that mailbox; we will coordinate a package (security whitepaper, NZ SOC2 bridge letter, vendor attestations).

E) Deletion detail we can commit to in contract:
- Immediate logical delete from runtime (seconds).
- Audit log entries referencing deletion actions retained per the account retention schedule (we can set to 90 days by default).
- Ability to request accelerated purge of backups: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to purge within 30 days; we can make this a contractual SLA for Dedicated/Private.

If you want formal contract language, I can circulate a short redline and a one-page appendix that your Legal team can attach to the Master Subscription Agreement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
